moat_against: Moats are narrow and per-business, not one wide portfolio moat — attackable one unit at a time
Organic growth only ~5-6%; compounding depends on perpetual fairly-priced M&A at rising deal multiples
AI-native tools could lower switching costs or let customers insource owned workflows
Technology Enabled Products is cyclical hardware, unlike the software core
Leverage is structural to the model (net debt 3.5x normalized OE, engine basis)
moat_for: Mission-critical systems of record across ~29 niche vertical leaders (Deltek, Vertafore, Aderant, CentralReach) with very high retention and sticky pricing
DAT freight marketplace — genuine two-sided network effects
Proprietary vertical data assets (DAT load-board data, Neptune installed metering base) feeding vertical AI features
Disciplined decentralized M&A model lifting acquired margins over three decades
Diversified across uncorrelated verticals — no single customer or product drives results
moat_justification: Portfolio of ~29 niche category leaders (Deltek, Vertafore, DAT, Neptune) selling mission-critical systems of record with very high retention, proprietary vertical data, and a proven decentralized M&A model that lifts acquired margins; capped at 7 because the moats are narrow and per-business, organic growth is only ~5-6% so compounding depends on perpetual fairly-priced acquisitions, AI-native tools could erode switching costs, and leverage is structural at 3.5x normalized OE.
